tagline: Offline Health Triage for ASHA Workers

risk_description.URGENT_REFERRAL: This patient needs URGENT medical attention. Refer to the nearest health facility IMMEDIATELY.
risk_description.CLINIC_VISIT: This patient should visit a health clinic within 24 hours for further assessment.
risk_description.HOME_CARE: This patient can be managed at home with basic care. Monitor symptoms and return if they worsen.

explanations.general_danger_signs: This child has a serious danger sign. Children with danger signs can get worse very quickly and may die if not treated immediately at a hospital. Please take the child to the nearest hospital right away.
explanations.severe_pneumonia: This child has signs of severe breathing difficulty. The chest is pulling in, which means the lungs are working very hard. This child needs medicine and oxygen at a hospital. Please refer immediately.
explanations.pneumonia: This child is breathing faster than normal, which may be a sign of chest infection. The child should see a doctor within one day to get the right medicine.
explanations.severe_dehydration: This child has lost too much water from the body due to diarrhoea. This is very dangerous. The child needs fluids given through a tube at the hospital. Please refer immediately.
explanations.some_dehydration: This child has some signs of water loss. The child should be given ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts) and taken to a clinic for further check.
explanations.severe_malnutrition: This child is severely underweight or has swelling in both feet from lack of nutrition. This is very serious and needs hospital treatment with special food and medicine.
explanations.severe_fever: This child has fever with a stiff neck or bulging soft spot on the head, which may be a sign of brain infection (meningitis). This is very dangerous. Please refer to hospital immediately.
explanations.fever_only: This child has fever. Give paracetamol for fever, give plenty of fluids, and take the child to a clinic if fever continues for more than 2 days.
explanations.measles_complications: This child has a rash with complications that may be from measles. These complications can be serious. Please take the child to a clinic for treatment.
explanations.very_severe_disease_newborn: This newborn baby has a very serious sign. Newborn babies are very delicate and can become very sick very quickly. The baby needs hospital care immediately. Keep the baby warm and refer right away.
explanations.local_infection_newborn: This newborn has signs of a skin or umbilical infection. This should be treated at a clinic with medicine to prevent it from spreading.
explanations.jaundice_newborn: This newborn's skin has turned yellow. While common, it should be checked by a doctor to make sure it is not severe.
explanations.low_weight_newborn: This newborn has low birth weight and needs extra care with feeding and warmth. Please take to a clinic for guidance.
explanations.pregnancy_danger: This pregnant woman has a DANGER sign. This could be life-threatening for the mother and baby. She must be taken to a hospital IMMEDIATELY. Do not wait.
explanations.pregnancy_warning: This pregnant woman has symptoms that should be checked by a doctor. Please visit the health clinic within one day.
explanations.pregnancy_normal: This pregnancy appears to be progressing normally. Continue regular antenatal check-ups, eat well, take iron-folic acid tablets, and rest adequately.
explanations.adult_danger: This person has a serious sign that needs urgent medical care. Please go to the nearest hospital immediately.
explanations.adult_warning: This person has symptoms that should be checked by a doctor. Please visit a health clinic soon.
explanations.home_care_default: Based on the symptoms described, home care should be sufficient. Rest, drink plenty of fluids, and eat well. If symptoms get worse or new symptoms appear, please visit a health clinic.

about.title: About Sahaayak Pro
about.description: Sahaayak Pro is an offline symptom-triage and referral decision-support tool designed for ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) workers in rural India.
protocols: WHO IMNCI (Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness) Chart Booklet, 2014 revision
ASHA Training Modules 6 & 7 (Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, India)
NFHS-5 (National Family Health Survey) health indicators
about.disclaimer: ⚠️ This is a prototype decision-support tool. It does NOT diagnose disease. All triage recommendations must be clinically validated before real-world use. Always follow your training and consult with your supervisor.
